title: Quaestiones selectae abbreviatae et ordinatae per alphabetum super quattuor libris Sententiarum Petri Lombardi Quodlibetisque Metaphysicae et De Anima. Ed: Johannes de Colonia
shelf_note: 1477 incunable of Scotist scholastic questions (Sentences, Metaphysics, De anima); scholastic theology and natural philosophy, adjacent to the library's early-modern-knowledge holdings. No collection is given.
structure_note: 785 of 788 pages translated; manuscript foliation (85, 163, 283) and signatures (i2, h, p) agree with the OCR page-num tags. Nothing structural stands out.

book_verdict: A real 1477 Scotus incunable on the right leaves, but flash-lite reads the heavy abbreviations poorly: each page has a meaning-reversing misreading (God's blessing through an unworthy minister lost, 'concordia' read as 'discordia', the devil given a wife) and p.591's translation drops its opening paragraph. Not citable as it stands.

title: Moninckx Atlas, vol. 2
shelf_note: 1686–1709 watercolour florilegium of the Amsterdam Hortus Medicus (Moninckx), with Latin polynomials and Dutch names; early modern botany, fits early modern science.
structure_note: Each record is a two-page opening (text leaf + plate), consistently, with plate numbers 11, 29, 30 agreeing with the page-num tags. Image 13 is a 1000 px thumbnail while 31–32 are 10,526 px masters, so resolution varies across the book.

image description tags the drawing as an engraving

tr_errors.source: Mozingo van Acosia.
tr_errors.english: Mozingo of Acosia.
tr_errors.problem: carries the misread authority name

book_verdict: Clean: the short Latin and Dutch plant names are transcribed and translated correctly against the plates, with one misread authority name (Acosta → 'Acosia'). Showable.

title: Artificium artis generalis - BSB Clm 28951
shelf_note: A Lullian Ars text in a Gothic cursive manuscript (BSB Clm 28951); Lullism belongs with the library's combinatorial and esoteric holdings.
structure_note: 196 pages, 192 OCR'd, 187 translated, so a handful are untranslated. 'published: Unknown' could be filled from the BSB catalogue. Foliation 24 and 73 agree with the OCR.

book_verdict: Right leaves, but this Gothic-cursive Lull is beyond flash-lite: the abbreviations are read as garble or normalised toward the expected (durans → deus, de partibus → de nihilo), and the translations stay fluent over it. An expert would flag p.147's 'whether goodness is God' series on sight.

title: Statutes on the governance of the Royal Hospital and Chapel of the Savoy, 1523
shelf_note: Statutes of Henry VII's Savoy hospital (a manuscript of 1523): English institutional and charitable history, outside the library's esoteric and early-science traditions. No collection is given to justify it.
structure_note: 88 pages, 83 translated. The OCR page-num tags follow marginal marks ('a3' read as 43; the chapter number '22' read as a page number), not a foliation, but this is cosmetic.

ocr_errors.problem: a marginal note invented by copying a line of the body
signature read as page number

other.note: the invented margin note is translated and shown as a marginal heading

ocr_errors.problem: hospitio/hospitali
'tunc' dropped

book_verdict: Clean and readable: the Savoy statutes are transcribed and translated faithfully, with one copied-in margin note. Its place on this shelf is doubtful, but not its quality.

title: Ad illustriss. p. Ven. Paulum Nanum Taruisii Praetorem praefectu[m]que liber
shelf_note: Neo-Latin encomiastic elegiacs to Paolo Nani, Venetian praetor of Treviso (Lignamine, c.1510): humanist occasional verse, not alchemy, Hermetica or early science. No collection is given.
structure_note: 50 pages, 48 translated; manuscript page numbers 9 and 15 and signature 'biii' agree with the OCR.

ocr_errors.problem: long-s 'insere' read as 'infere'

ocr_errors.image: Et rigidos mores ingenium que gr[a]tie (overwritten, partly illegible)
ocr_errors.problem: the end of the line is a scribal correction; 'ferox' is not legible on the leaf and may be supplied
'fosso' read as 'follo'

tr_errors.source: Me lepus, et follo latitans que Cuniculus antro / Plus animi, & passus rectia ceruus habet
tr_errors.english: The hare, and the rabbit hiding in a hollow cave, / Has more heart, and the deer has more steps.
tr_errors.problem: 'Me' (than me) dropped: the poet says even a hare, a rabbit and a netted stag have more spirit than he; the comparison and the point of the stanza are lost, and 'passus retia' (that has suffered nets) becomes 'more steps'

other.note: '<meta>Decorative black square initials ...</meta>' and <summary>/<keywords> blocks in the translation pane

ocr_errors.problem: 'Praetores' given as 'Pratores'

book_verdict: A clean humanist-hand manuscript of praise poems, accurately transcribed and translated apart from one lost comparison on p.14 (the 'me' in 'Me lepus'). Good text, doubtful shelf.
